findings.claim: TRUNK-6701 asks for two things and this PR does one: 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, AND remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute.' The INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID write at OpenmrsFilter.java:64 is byte-identical to the base and is not mentioned anywhere in the PR body, yet the ticket is now Closed/Done. The omission is almost certainly the correct engineering call (the ticket's premise that nothing reads the attribute is false once legacyui is installed), but nothing on the PR or the ticket records that, so the next person who reads TRUNK-6701 as complete can ship the deletion the ticket still asks for.
findings.evidence: TICKET (https://openmrs.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/TRUNK-6701): Background says the filter 'stores a per-request timestamp attribute that nothing in core reads'; Requested change says 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, and remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute.' Status is Closed / Done with ibacher's merge+backport comment (2026-09-12). DIFF: `git diff eda229b12a28a41ba35ecd75b910803da93631a8 d381957e84386f5902bec7886b8f2ba391dc5101 -- web/.../OpenmrsFilter.java` has no hunk covering line 64; base line 63 and head line 64 are the same `httpRequest.setAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID, String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis()));`. The PR body's 'Changes' list makes no mention of it. WHY REMOVING IT WOULD BE WRONG (the part that makes this worth saying rather than dropping): `git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID` in openmrs-core returns exactly two hits, the WebConstants declaration and this write, with no read (positive control: `git grep -c OPENMRS_USER_CONTEXT_HTTPSESSION_ATTR` returns hits in 3 files, so the pipeline finds what is there). But the readers are downstream: `gh api search/code q='INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID repo:openmrs/openmrs-module-legacyui'` returns total_count 3, and fetching the blobs at ref da89912c82ecc7f52e74c66fbfd779000c933414 shows HtmlIncludeTag.java:160 `pageRequest.getAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID)` (logs log.error when absent) and PortletController.java:111-113 `String uniqueRequestId = (String) request.getAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID); ... if (uniqueRequestId.equals(lastRequestId))` -- an unguarded dereference that NPEs on every portlet render if the attribute is gone. Also note the attribute is a REQUEST attribute (httpRequest.setAttribute), not a session one, so it is never replicated and costs one currentTimeMillis plus one map put per request; the ticket grouped it with the session-dirty problem, but it is not one. ANCHORING NOTE for the merge agent: line 64 is outside both diff hunks (hunk 2 covers RIGHT lines 72-97), so this cannot be anchored as an inline diff comment at 64 -- either anchor near line 93/94 (where the ticket's other requested change lands) or carry it as the one body-worthy item. ASK: not a code change -- say on the PR/ticket that the unique-id half is deliberately not done because legacyui's HtmlIncludeTag and PortletController read it, so TRUNK-6701 is not silently closed with a live request that a follow-up would implement.

what_i_swept: Step 2 in full at d381957e84386f5902bec7886b8f2ba391dc5101. (1) Authority: no linked GitHub issue (closingIssuesReferences empty); read TRUNK-6701 with both its comments via the unauthenticated JIRA REST endpoint, plus the PR body's own 'Changes' list. (2) Does it resolve the problem: ran the reported problem as an experiment rather than reading it. `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` is 5/5 green at head; I then checked the BASE production file into the worktree (`git checkout eda229b1 -- web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java`) and re-ran: 3 of 5 fail -- shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymousSessionAttributes:113 expected 0 but was 1, shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes:181 expected 0 but was 2, shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale:143 expected 1 but was 2. Note which assertions did NOT fail on base: every value assertion (lines 139-140, 177-178, etc.) passed on both base and head, which is direct empirical confirmation of the ticket's first acceptance criterion ('session attributes end up with the same values as today'), and the countWrites failures confirm the second ('no attribute writes occur when values are unchanged'). Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`; `git status --porcelain` empty and the file md5 matches `git show d381957e:...` (679b22d432987691b2f2a4a945a02265). (3) Does it do only that: accounted for every hunk -- the `java.util.Objects` import, the if/else restructure (required by the ticket's Background, which names the anonymous-then-overwrite write), the helper, the test class and its dataset (required by AC 'tests cover both user states'). The one non-required byte is a two-line comment joined into one at head line 75, inside an otherwise-required hunk; not worth raising. No format sweep, no drive-by rename, no unrelated file. (4) Best available fix: named and weighed the alternatives -- (a) the private setSessionAttributeIfChanged helper as shipped; (b) stop writing username/locale to the session entirely and let consumers read UserContext, rejected because the unchanged comment at head line 88-89 says the attributes exist 'so parent servlet container can identify sessions easier' and downstream JSPs read sessionScope; (c) hoist the helper into FilterUtil/WebUtil as a static so InitializationFilter and UpdateFilter could share it -- rejected as a finding because those two are setup-wizard filters that short-circuit on a running system (webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml lines 102 and 112), so there is no second per-request caller and the abstraction would be built for a case that does not exist; (d) use the existing FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE constant instead of the "locale" literal -- rejected, and worth recording that it would have been a WRONG suggestion: that constant names a session key the wizard filters fill with a String (UpdateFilter.java:295 `locale.toString()`), while OpenmrsFilter stores a Locale object, so the two are not the same contract despite the identical key. On house conventions for the comparison itself, `Objects.equals` already appears in api/src/main/java (AdministrationServiceImpl, ModuleConditionalResource, DatabaseUpdater), so the JDK call is in-tree, not a divergence from the older OpenmrsUtil.nullSafeEquals. I therefore have no approach objection and say nothing about the approach. OUTWARD TRACE (one level out, in-dimension): (i) behaviour-equivalence of moving getAuthenticatedUser() out of the else branch -- read UserContext.java:107-109, the constructor only assigns authenticationScheme and leaves `private User user = null` (line 69), and getAuthenticatedUser() (line 211) is a bare field read, so a freshly created context still yields the anonymous name; (ii) the only observable change is the NUMBER of setAttribute calls, so the consumers that could break are ones reacting to the write event, not the value -- `git grep HttpSessionAttributeListener|HttpSessionBindingListener|attributeReplaced|attributeAdded` over core returns zero (positive control: the same grep finds HttpSessionListener in web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java), and `gh api search/code q='HttpSessionAttributeListener repo:openmrs/openmrs-module-legacyui'` returns total_count 0 (positive control: the same query for INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID on that repo returns 3), while legacyui's CurrentUsers keys a servletContext map driven explicitly by LoginServlet rather than by attribute events -- so nothing observes the suppressed writes; (iii) other writers of the same keys -- broad `git grep '\.setAttribute('` over web/src/main/java shows OpenmrsFilter is the only per-request session writer in core; legacyui's LoginServlet changes locale via Context.setLocale (mutating the UserContext), which the next request's filter correctly detects as changed; (iv) unchanged neighbours stating assumptions -- the web.xml comment at line 148 ('This filter should come before the OpenmrsFilter, i.e., before we've created a session') stays true because head line 61 httpRequest.getSession() is untouched, satisfying the ticket's 'session creation behavior is intentionally out of scope'; the in-file comment at head lines 71-72 about logic 'copied to webinf/view/uncaughtexception.jsp' also stays true, because I fetched legacyui's uncaughtException.jsp and it only re-reads OPENMRS_USER_CONTEXT_HTTPSESSION_ATTR (line 23) and never duplicates the username/locale writes.

out_of_scope: conventions/correctness: FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE (web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/util/FilterUtil.java:36) is the literal "locale", and InitializationFilter/UpdateFilter write a String into that session key (UpdateFilter.java:295 locale.toString()) while OpenmrsFilter writes a Locale object into the same key -- a pre-existing type collision on one session attribute, untouched by this PR but now also the subject of an equality comparison.

conventions/docs: the unchanged comment at OpenmrsFilter.java:71-72 points at 'webinf/view/uncaughtexception.jsp', which does not exist in openmrs-core (find returns nothing); it lives in legacyui at omod/src/main/webapp/uncaughtException.jsp with different casing and path.
conventions: setSessionAttributeIfChanged (OpenmrsFilter.java:122) uses no instance state and could be private static.

test coverage: RecordingHttpSession.countWrites (OpenmrsFilterTest.java:236) counts writes by attribute NAME only and ignores the value, so it would not catch a write of a wrong value that happened the right number of times.

test coverage: the new web/src/test/resources/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml duplicates a test_user row (same password hash and salt) that already exists in api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/api/include/EncounterServiceTest-initialData.xml.

correctness (pre-existing, unchanged by the PR): User.getUsername() can be null for users identified only by systemId, in which case setAttribute(name, null) removes the session attribute entirely rather than falling back to the anonymous placeholder -- identical on base and head, so not a regression.
could_not_verify: I could not exercise a real replicating/clustered session manager (Tomcat DeltaManager, Spring Session) to confirm that the reduced setAttribute count actually reduces replication traffic. I verified only the write-count reduction itself, empirically, via the base-vs-head test run described above; the replication benefit is inferred from the servlet contract rather than measured.

The legacyui evidence (HtmlIncludeTag.java:160, PortletController.java:111-113, uncaughtException.jsp, CurrentUsers.java) comes from GitHub's contents API at ref da89912c82ecc7f52e74c66fbfd779000c933414, not from a local checkout or a build of legacyui against this core sha. raw.githubusercontent.com returned empty for these paths in this environment, so I used `gh api .../contents/<path>?ref=<sha>` and base64-decoded; the INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID lines quoted are the decoded file contents, not a search snippet.
